title: Climb out of gravity's well
hook: Change distance from the centre and predict gravitational-potential magnitude.
misconception: gravitational-potential magnitude doubles when distance from the centre doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply potential magnitude = GM/r to compare gravitational-potential magnitude when distance from the centre changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed spherical mass with potential set to zero at infinity, potential magnitude = GM/r. When distance from the centre doubles, gravitational-potential magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model potential magnitude = GM/r; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed spherical mass with potential set to zero at infinity, with a nonzero initial result. If distance from the centre triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on gravitational-potential magnitude?
recall.why: Apply potential magnitude = GM/r under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
